clue.text: Opposition badly resents CIA

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and disordered, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A political opponent bitterly resents the American intelligence agency.
explanation.definitionFit: Resistance is the act of standing against something, the same idea as opposition to it.

clue.text: Nervous pirate holds back tears

indicators.note: going back means the concealed letters are read from right to left
the words are said to hold the answer, so it sits inside their run of letters

parts.note: found across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: An anxious buccaneer is fighting back tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tears' reads as weeping, but the answer is the verb sense: tears as in rends cloth, giving RIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To tear something is to rip it, so tears and rips are synonyms as verbs.

clue.text: Instrument trapped spirit

parts.note: to snare an animal is to trap it
rum is a spirit, an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: A musical instrument with a ghost caught inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A snare drum is a percussion instrument with wires stretched under it.

clue.text: Small catch for one constantly moving home?

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small
to nail a criminal is to catch them

explanation.surface: A modest prize for someone who keeps relocating house.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the shell a snail carries everywhere, so its home moves whenever it does.
explanation.definitionFit: A snail carries its shell on its back, so wherever it crawls its dwelling travels too.

clue.text: Able seamen trick Democrat and run away

parts.note: AB is an able seaman, so two of them are ABS
a con is a swindle or trick
D is the abbreviation for a Democrat

explanation.surface: Sailors swindle an American politician and then flee.
explanation.definitionFit: To abscond is to leave hurriedly and secretly, usually to escape something, which is running away.

clue.text: Abundant debt hidden by policemen

indicators.note: something hidden by another thing is wrapped up inside it

parts.note: cops is slang for police officers
an IOU is a written acknowledgment of a debt

explanation.surface: A large sum owed is being concealed by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Copious means plentiful, existing in large quantities, the same as abundant.

clue.text: Place where soldiers eat the edges of marmite sandwiches

indicators.note: edges are the outermost parts, so only the first and final letters of each word are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A spot where troops eat the crusts of their yeast-spread sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: Marmite is a salty yeast-extract spread popular in Britain, eaten on toast or in sandwiches.
explanation.definitionFit: A mess is the dining hall of a military unit, where service personnel take their meals.

clue.text: Background actor's partner once picked up painting?

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner

indicators.note: in a down clue, picking something up lifts it so its letters read from the bottom upward

parts.note: painting is an example of art

explanation.surface: An actor's former lover collects a picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts a solver toward a sound-alike, but in a down clue it lifts the word upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is a film or TV performer hired to fill the background of a scene without lines.

clue.text: Bursars got confused in European city

indicators.note: confused letters are muddled up and must be put into a new order

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: College treasurers lost their way on a trip to the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: A bursar is the treasurer of a school or college.
explanation.definitionFit: Strasbourg is a city in eastern France, seat of the European Parliament.

clue.text: What soup is cooked for boxer?

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so these letters are mixed into something new

parts.note: the eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A question about which broth is being made for a fighter's dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What' looks like the start of a question, but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A southpaw is a left-handed boxer, so the general word boxer covers it as a definition by example.

clue.text: Quiet and idle, briefly by a public square

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
idle means lazy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sits silent and lazy for a while beside a town square.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaza is an open public space in a town, the Spanish term for a square.

clue.text: Fan has one drink, then another

parts.note: a sup is a single mouthful of drink
porter is a dark beer, another drink

explanation.surface: A sports fan downs one drink after another.
explanation.definitionFit: A supporter of a team is an enthusiast or follower, which is what a fan is.

clue.text: Rich source of water also containing diamonds

parts.note: a well is a source of water drawn from underground

indicators.note: containing means the preceding word wraps around the one after it

parts.note: also and too are synonyms
D is the abbreviation for the card suit diamonds

explanation.surface: A wealthy spring of water that also holds gemstones.
explanation.definitionFit: Well-to-do is an idiom for prosperous or affluent, the same as rich.

clue.text: Electric vehicles fashionable, in retrospect

indicators.note: retrospect means looking backward, so the word is read from its end to its start

parts.note: smart clothes are stylish and fashionable

explanation.surface: Battery cars were trendy, looking back on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Trams are passenger vehicles running on rails, usually powered from overhead electric cables.

clue.text: Perhaps how Humpty Dumpty fell is crazy

definitions.meaning: first meaning: literally, down from where he sat in the nursery rhyme
second meaning: eccentric, bizarre or unconventional

explanation.surface: Suggests that the nursery-rhyme egg's tumble was madness.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme, Humpty Dumpty sat on a wall and had a great fall; 'perhaps' flags that the rhyme never says exactly how.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an informal idiom for wildly unconventional, and also literally describes tumbling from the wall in the rhyme.

clue.text: Impudent old president keeps fighting

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it within, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: Gerald Ford was a past US president
war is armed fighting

explanation.surface: A cheeky former head of state goes on waging battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Forward can mean presumptuous or overly bold in manner, much like impudent or cheeky.

clue.text: States working to limit current antipathy

indicators.note: to limit something is to set boundaries around it, so these words enclose the next

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
I is the symbol for electric current
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: Governments acting to restrain modern hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: The enclosing letters are both of the first two words together, with the current slipped in between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Aversion is a strong dislike, the same feeling as antipathy.

clue.text: Boss is certainly flash, drinking a tiny bit of port

indicators.note: something drinking takes a liquid inside itself, so it surrounds the next piece

parts.note: sure as an exclamation means certainly

indicators.note: a tiny bit of a word is just its opening letter

parts.note: first letter of the word
a mo is a moment, as is a flash

explanation.surface: The chief is surely showy, sipping a drop of fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: The port drop goes inside the word for certainly; the word for flash follows. 'Flash' as showy is the trap: it means an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: A supremo is the person in overall charge of an organisation, an informal word for a boss.

clue.text: Skilled workers in Niger seen messing around

indicators.note: messing around with things puts them in disorder, so the letters get shuffled about

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Tradespeople in a West African country are spotted fooling about.
explanation.definitionFit: Engineers are trained technical professionals who design, build or maintain machines and structures.

clue.text: English politician interrupts trial, causing a storm

indicators.note: to interrupt something is to break into the middle of it, so these letters go inside

parts.note: a trial is a test
E is the abbreviation for English
an MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A British lawmaker disrupts a court case and stirs up an uproar.
explanation.definitionFit: A tempest is a violent windy storm, a literary synonym.

clue.text: Russian empress bought sari, naturally reduced

indicators.note: the words are reduced by trimming letters from both ends, leaving a run from within them

parts.note: a run of letters spanning all three words

explanation.surface: A Russian royal purchased an Indian garment, at a discount of course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduced' plays on a sale price, but it trims the phrase from both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsarina was the wife of a tsar or a woman ruling Russia herself, an empress.

clue.text: Wealthy lady bet on party

indicators.note: in an across clue, one thing placed on another comes after it, so the second-named piece goes first

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a wager is a bet

explanation.surface: A rich woman gambles on a political faction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' looks political, but it is a social gathering; in an across clue the bet sits on, after, the party.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding property or title from her late husband, so typically a rich elderly woman.

clue.text: Ordered extremely decisive statement of belief

indicators.note: extremely here means at the extremes, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word
a creed is a formal statement of religious belief

explanation.surface: A command issued as a very firm declaration of faith.
explanation.definitionFit: To decree is to order something by official authority, so decreed means ordered.

clue.text: At first, everyone likes very entertaining, silly magical creatures

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of each of the words that follow

parts.note: first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Initially, all people enjoy really funny, daft fairy-tale beings.
explanation.definitionFit: Elves are small supernatural beings from folklore, a kind of magical creature.

clue.text: Important talk cut short after six

indicators.note: something cut short has its end chopped off, losing the final letter

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
taken as written

explanation.surface: A key speech gets trimmed once it passes six o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: Vital means essential or of great significance, a close synonym of important.

clue.text: On your own, capturing top gangster

indicators.note: capturing something means holding it inside, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: on your own means alone
a cap is a top or lid

explanation.surface: Working solo, someone seizes the leading crime boss.
explanation.definitionFit: Al Capone was the notorious Chicago gangster of the Prohibition era.

clue.text: Unhealthy-looking food from Cornwall?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: pale and sickly in complexion
second meaning: a baked pastry case with a savoury filling

explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is a county in south-west England famous for its meat-and-vegetable pastries; the question mark marks the second sense as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for a pallid complexion and also a noun for the Cornish filled pastry turnover.

clue.text: Candid old writer

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.walkthrough: 'Writer' suggests an author, but it is the tool that writes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone open is frank and honest, holding nothing back, which is what candid means.

clue.text: Art house I renovated gets sanction

indicators.note: renovating rebuilds something into a new form, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A cinema showing independent films is refurbished with official approval.
explanation.definitionFit: To sanction is to give official permission for something, the same as to authorise it.

clue.text: Turning around, strips — you do it in bed

indicators.note: turning around faces the other way, so the word is read from its last letter back

parts.note: to peel is to strip off an outer layer

explanation.surface: Someone spins round, undresses, then climbs into bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface hints at something racy in bed, but the definition is innocent.
explanation.definitionFit: The cryptic definition describes the main activity of bedtime, resting with eyes closed through the night.

clue.text: John twice heard Scottish singer

indicators.note: heard means the clue words are taken by their spoken sound, not their spelling

parts.note: john is American slang for a toilet, a loo, said two times

explanation.surface: A man named John was overheard twice by a Glaswegian vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: John looks like a name, but it is slang for a toilet; loo is the everyday British word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lulu is a Glasgow-born pop singer known for Shout and a Eurovision win in 1969.

clue.text: Spotted young man touring India and Spain, flipping inquisitive

indicators.note: touring a place means travelling all round it, so one word surrounds another

parts.note: a lad is a boy or young man
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: flipping something over turns it the other way, so the word is read backward

parts.note: nosey means prying or inquisitive

explanation.surface: A curious boy travelling round India and Spain was noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Only India goes inside the young man; Spain follows, then the reversed word.
explanation.definitionFit: To lay eyes on someone is to see them, so laid eyes on means spotted, in the past tense.
